documents.title: Short-read quality control and filtering

metrics.name: Q20/Q30 rate
metrics.meaning: Fraction of bases whose reported Phred quality is at least the named threshold; it summarizes base-call confidence, not biological validity.

metrics.name: reads/bases retained
metrics.meaning: Amount retained after configured filtering and trimming. Large losses require inspection of adapters, quality, minimum length, and input quality.

metrics.name: GC content
metrics.meaning: Base-composition summary. A shift after filtering can reflect removal of contaminants or biased filtering, but is not diagnostic on its own.

metrics.name: duplication rate
metrics.meaning: Repeated read content; it can reflect PCR duplication, high coverage, low-complexity sequence, or genuinely abundant organisms.

interpretation: Compare before- and after-filtering counts, quality profiles, adapter content, length distribution, and GC together.
For metagenomes, unusual or multimodal GC and duplication can be biological consequences of mixed organisms, so isolate-style rules should not be applied mechanically.
MultiQC aggregates upstream reports and does not perform a new biological analysis.
caveats: Phred scores are sequencer estimates and may be platform- or run-dependent.
Aggressive trimming can shorten reads and reduce downstream assembly continuity even when mean quality improves.
Passing QC does not establish sample identity, purity, or sufficient depth.

documents.title: Long-read NanoStat, NanoPlot and nanoq interpretation

metrics.name: read N50
metrics.meaning: Length such that half of sequenced bases are in reads at least that long; it measures the read-length distribution, not assembly quality.

metrics.name: total yield
metrics.meaning: Total sequenced bases. Interpret relative to target genome size or metagenome complexity and coverage requirements.

metrics.name: mean/median read quality
metrics.meaning: Summary of reported per-read quality; distributions and low-quality tails remain important.

interpretation: Compare NanoStat on raw input with NanoStat on nanoq output to quantify the exact yield/length cost and quality gain from filtering.
Longer reads aid repeat resolution and scaffolding, while sufficient accurate yield supports polishing and low-abundance recovery.
caveats: Read N50 can increase merely because short reads were removed; always report retained yield alongside it.
A single average quality value can hide broad or multimodal distributions.
Long-read quality encodings and calibration depend on platform/basecaller.

documents.title: Genome and metagenome assembly interpretation

metrics.name: N50/L50
metrics.meaning: Length/count summaries of contiguity. Higher N50 or lower L50 does not establish correctness, completeness, or absence of collapsed repeats.

metrics.name: total assembly length
metrics.meaning: Sum of assembled bases; compare with expected genome size for isolates, but mixed metagenomes do not have one expected genome size.

metrics.name: number of contigs
metrics.meaning: Fragmentation summary that depends strongly on the minimum contig length used for reporting.

metrics.name: misassemblies/genome fraction
metrics.meaning: Reference-based quantities when an appropriate reference is supplied; reference divergence can affect both.

interpretation: Assess contiguity together with mapping support, depth uniformity, genome quality, taxonomy, and contamination checks.
Assemblers optimize different data types: SPAdes and MEGAHIT use short reads, Flye targets long reads, while Unicycler and OPERA-MS combine read types in hybrid workflows.
caveats: N50 is not comparable when assemblies use different length cutoffs without checking the reporting configuration.
A very contiguous assembly can still contain chimeras, collapsed repeats, contamination, or polishing errors.
Reference-based QUAST statistics are limited by reference choice and completeness.

documents.title: Read mapping, depth and breadth of coverage

metrics.name: mapping rate
metrics.meaning: Fraction of reads aligned under the chosen mapper and parameters; it is affected by divergence, filtering, multi-mapping, and reference composition.

metrics.name: depth
metrics.meaning: Number of aligned read bases/reads covering positions. Uneven profiles may indicate repeats, copy-number variation, contamination, assembly errors, or ecological abundance differences.

metrics.name: breadth
metrics.meaning: Fraction of sequence covered at a specified minimum depth; report the threshold because breadth changes with it.

metrics.name: properly paired
metrics.meaning: Paired reads satisfying aligner/library orientation expectations, useful for short-read assembly support.

interpretation: Use mapping rate, breadth, depth distribution, and pair/orientation statistics together rather than relying on mean depth.
In metagenomes, depth also reflects organism abundance and strain mixture, so non-uniformity is not automatically an assembly defect.
caveats: Multi-mapping reads in conserved or repeated regions can inflate or redistribute coverage depending on settings.
Mean depth can conceal uncovered regions and extreme peaks.
Coverage supports but does not prove correctness or biological presence without appropriate controls.

documents.title: Metagenome binning and consensus bin selection

metrics.name: bin count
metrics.meaning: Number of candidate genome bins; more bins do not necessarily mean more high-quality or non-redundant genomes.

metrics.name: bin score
metrics.meaning: Tool-specific objective used to select bins, commonly combining completeness and contamination estimates; it is not a universal quality metric.

metrics.name: coverage/composition separation
metrics.meaning: Binners use abundance and/or sequence-composition signals, whose separability depends on samples, strain complexity, and assembly fragmentation.

interpretation: DAS Tool integrates candidate bins from multiple methods and selects a non-redundant set; evaluate the selected bins downstream with quality, taxonomy, and chimerism checks.
SemiBin2 can use learned sequence features with coverage information; GPU acceleration affects runtime, not the biological meaning of results.
caveats: Closely related strains, mobile elements, shared repeats, uneven depth, and short contigs are major causes of mixed or incomplete bins.
Binning output is a hypothesis about genome membership, not a validated isolate genome.
Tool-specific scores should not be compared across algorithms as if calibrated identically.

documents.title: Genome and MAG completeness, contamination and MIMAG quality

metrics.name: completeness
metrics.meaning: Estimated recovery of expected genome content from marker/model evidence; interpretation depends on lineage representation and the estimator.

metrics.name: contamination
metrics.meaning: Estimated duplicated or foreign genome content; strain heterogeneity and unusual biology can influence the estimate.

metrics.name: BUSCO complete/single-copy/duplicated
metrics.meaning: Status of lineage-specific conserved orthologs, useful for genome/gene-set assessment but not a direct contamination or correctness measurement.

interpretation: Use completeness and contamination as estimates, and cross-check discordant genomes with mapping, taxonomy, GUNC, assembly structure, and marker details.
MIMAG high-quality drafts require more than completeness/contamination, including defined rRNA and tRNA criteria and supporting metadata; do not assign that label from CheckM2 alone.
caveats: Marker-based estimates can be biased for underrepresented, reduced, unusual, or highly divergent lineages.
A nominal quality tier does not establish assembly correctness or biological purity.
CheckM2 predictions are model estimates and should retain tool/database version provenance.

documents.title: GUNC lineage-consistency and chimerism assessment

metrics.name: pass.GUNC
metrics.meaning: Tool decision derived from lineage-homogeneity statistics and configured thresholds; inspect the contributing metrics rather than treating it as infallible.

metrics.name: clade separation score
metrics.meaning: Degree to which genes split across taxonomic lineages at the reported taxonomic level.

metrics.name: reference representation score
metrics.meaning: How sufficiently the genome's genes map to the reference system for interpretation.

metrics.name: contamination portion
metrics.meaning: Estimated portion attributed to the inferred contaminating lineage signal.

interpretation: A fail is evidence of lineage inconsistency compatible with a chimeric/contaminated bin and should prompt gene/contig-level inspection and possible bin refinement.
The Sankey view should be used to locate the taxonomic level and lineages contributing to inconsistency.
caveats: Low reference representation or too few mapped genes can make a genome difficult or impossible to score reliably.
Horizontal gene transfer, mobile elements, and database gaps can create lineage discordance that needs biological review.
GUNC complements rather than replaces completeness/contamination estimators.

documents.title: Genome taxonomy with GTDB-Tk, FastANI and marker evidence

metrics.name: classification
metrics.meaning: GTDB taxonomic assignment produced from reference-tree placement, relative evolutionary divergence, ANI and alignment fraction under the installed release.

metrics.name: fast ANI
metrics.meaning: Approximate nucleotide identity over homologous genomic regions; interpret with alignment fraction and assembly quality.

metrics.name: alignment fraction
metrics.meaning: Fraction represented by ANI-matched regions and essential context for similarity interpretation.

metrics.name: warnings/note
metrics.meaning: Flags conditions such as low marker recovery, multiple placements, or other limitations that can affect classification confidence.

interpretation: Report GTDB release and inspect classification method, closest reference, ANI, alignment fraction, tree placement, and warnings together.
Use 16S/BLAST or other marker evidence as complementary evidence, not as an automatic override of genome-wide classification.
caveats: Taxonomic names and placements can change across GTDB/database releases.
Low-quality, incomplete, contaminated, or chimeric genomes can be misclassified or remain unresolved.
ANI calculated over limited aligned sequence can look high without broad genomic support.

documents.title: Read-based taxonomic profiling and abundance

metrics.name: relative abundance
metrics.meaning: Within-sample proportion assigned by a method; values are compositional and dependent on marker/reference databases and filtering.

metrics.name: classified/unclassified reads
metrics.meaning: Fractions with or without assignments under the selected database and confidence settings; unclassified does not mean biologically unknown in an absolute sense.

metrics.name: taxonomic rank
metrics.meaning: Resolution of an assignment. Species-level calls need sufficient discriminating evidence and are usually less robust than higher ranks.

interpretation: MetaPhlAn estimates clade abundance from marker genes; Kraken2 classifies k-mers and Bracken re-estimates abundance from Kraken classifications, so their percentages are not interchangeable.
Focus on dominant and reproducible patterns, controls, read support, and agreement across methods when available.
caveats: Relative abundance is not absolute cell count, biomass, load, or activity.
Database content/version, closely related taxa, contamination, and host depletion strongly affect profiles.
Non-detection does not prove absence, especially for low-abundance organisms.

documents.title: MAG abundance and coverage with CoverM

metrics.name: mean/trimmed mean coverage
metrics.meaning: Average depth across a genome after the tool's configured filtering/trimming; susceptibility to uncovered regions and peaks differs by statistic.

metrics.name: covered fraction
metrics.meaning: Fraction of genome positions meeting coverage requirements; useful for distinguishing broad support from small conserved-region matches.

metrics.name: relative abundance
metrics.meaning: CoverM-normalized within-sample abundance based on mapped reads and selected calculation; retain method and mapping thresholds.

metrics.name: TPM/RPKM
metrics.meaning: Length/library-normalized mapping quantities, not direct cell counts and not automatically comparable across workflows.

interpretation: Interpret abundance only for quality-controlled, non-redundant MAGs and require adequate breadth to avoid over-interpreting sparse conserved-region mappings.
Use consistent mapper, identity, alignment, and normalization settings for comparisons.
caveats: Multi-mapping among related MAGs and strain variation can distort abundance.
Genome size, copy-number variation, extraction bias, and sequencing bias prevent direct translation to cell counts.
A single sample cannot establish a statistically supported ecological difference.

documents.title: Within-sample alpha diversity
typical_outputs: alpha-diversity summary computed from a taxonomic abundance table

metrics.name: richness
metrics.meaning: Number of detected taxa after the chosen filtering and rank; highly sensitive to depth, classification noise, and thresholding.

metrics.name: Shannon index
metrics.meaning: Combines richness and evenness using taxon proportions; the value depends on logarithm convention and taxonomic resolution.

metrics.name: Simpson index
metrics.meaning: Family of dominance/diversity quantities with multiple conventions; the exact formula must be stated before comparing values.

interpretation: Use alpha diversity to describe one profile, not to claim a treatment or group effect without replicated samples and statistical design.
Comparisons require consistent depth handling, taxonomic rank, database, filters, and index definitions.
caveats: A higher index is not inherently healthier or better; meaning is ecosystem- and question-specific.
Classification errors and rare low-support taxa can inflate richness.
Read-based and MAG-based diversity describe different observable subsets and should not be directly equated.

documents.title: Nonpareil metagenomic redundancy and coverage

metrics.name: estimated coverage
metrics.meaning: Model-based estimate of the fraction of sequence space represented at the observed effort.

metrics.name: Nonpareil diversity
metrics.meaning: Sequence-level diversity estimate derived from read redundancy, not a taxon-count index.

metrics.name: projected effort
metrics.meaning: Model projection of additional sequencing needed for target coverage; uncertainty grows outside the observed range.

interpretation: Use the curve to assess diminishing returns and whether the sample's sequence diversity is well represented by current sequencing effort.
Compare samples only under compatible preprocessing, read lengths, and model settings.
caveats: Coverage is model-based and not the same as mean mapping depth or the fraction of organisms detected.
Extrapolated sequencing requirements are uncertain, especially for highly complex or uneven communities.
Technical duplicates, host reads, and preprocessing can alter redundancy.

documents.title: Structural genome annotation with Prokka, Prodigal and barrnap

metrics.name: CDS count
metrics.meaning: Number of predicted coding sequences under the gene caller and contig context; fragmentation can split or truncate genes.

metrics.name: hypothetical proteins
metrics.meaning: Predicted proteins without a confident named function in the annotation hierarchy; not necessarily novel or nonfunctional.

metrics.name: rRNA/tRNA count
metrics.meaning: Detected structural RNA features; absence can reflect incompleteness, assembly fragmentation, or detection limits.

interpretation: Use feature counts as assembly/annotation summaries and inspect individual annotations with coordinates, evidence, and protein/domain results.
A genome browser shows genomic context and synteny that counts alone cannot capture.
caveats: Automated names are database- and rule-dependent predictions, not experimental functional validation.
Contig-edge genes, frameshifts, polishing errors, and divergent proteins can be missed or misannotated.
Annotation database and software versions are essential provenance.

documents.title: Protein domains, orthology and pathway annotation

metrics.name: domain/signature hit
metrics.meaning: Sequence match to a member database signature. Coverage, score, e-value, and domain architecture determine how informative it is.

metrics.name: ortholog/COG category
metrics.meaning: Function transferred through inferred orthology or orthologous group membership; broad categories summarize potential rather than precise activity.

metrics.name: KO assignment
metrics.meaning: KEGG Orthology prediction using profile thresholds; pathway reconstruction generally requires combinations of KOs.

interpretation: Prefer concordant evidence from curated orthology, domain architecture, and pathway completeness over a single weak hit.
Use pathway/module context to distinguish an isolated homolog from a more complete encoded capability.
caveats: All are sequence-based predictions of encoded potential, not gene expression, enzyme activity, flux, or phenotype.
Paralogs, multidomain proteins, partial genes, and remote homology can produce ambiguous assignments.
Database release and score/coverage thresholds affect counts and labels.

documents.title: Carbohydrate-active enzyme annotation with dbCAN

metrics.name: CAZyme family
metrics.meaning: Predicted membership in a carbohydrate-active enzyme family; family membership may encompass multiple substrates or activities.

metrics.name: tool support
metrics.meaning: Agreement among HMM/database/subfamily methods. Multiple methods can increase confidence but are not independent experimental validations.

metrics.name: gene cluster
metrics.meaning: Genomic neighborhood consistent with coordinated carbohydrate utilization; context strengthens but does not prove a specific substrate phenotype.

interpretation: Interpret family composition with genome size/completeness and examine subfamily or gene-cluster context before assigning a substrate or reaction.
For MAG comparisons, normalize and filter consistently and avoid treating raw family counts as direct activities.
caveats: A CAZy family hit indicates sequence similarity and potential, not expression, secretion, substrate use, or measured degradation.
Partial genes and assembly fragmentation can reduce or split hits.
Substrate predictions can be broad or uncertain.

documents.title: Acquired antimicrobial-resistance gene screening

metrics.name: percent identity
metrics.meaning: Sequence identity between the assembled query region and database reference over the reported alignment.

metrics.name: percent coverage
metrics.meaning: Fraction of the reference resistance gene covered by the hit; truncated hits need careful review.

metrics.name: database/gene
metrics.meaning: Reference collection and allele/family label supporting the reported match.

interpretation: Prioritize high-quality, well-covered hits, then inspect genomic context, assembly support, gene integrity, database provenance, and organism relevance.
Report detected acquired resistance determinants as genomic predictions requiring appropriate confirmation.
caveats: ABRicate searches assembled contigs for acquired genes and does not comprehensively detect chromosomal point mutations, regulatory resistance, expression, or susceptibility phenotype.
A gene hit must not be translated directly into a clinical treatment recommendation.
Database scope/version and assembly fragmentation affect detection.

documents.title: CRISPR-Cas subtype and locus architecture

metrics.name: predicted subtype
metrics.meaning: Classification inferred from Cas protein profiles and locus organization.

metrics.name: locus completeness
metrics.meaning: Presence/order of expected components; partial contigs and fragmented assemblies can truncate systems.

metrics.name: array/spacer count
metrics.meaning: Detected CRISPR repeat-spacer structures under tool thresholds; counts can vary with assembly and repeat detection.

interpretation: Use the gene/synteny map to assess whether Cas genes form a coherent locus and whether the predicted subtype matches the component order.
Inspect partial or mixed loci cautiously, particularly at contig boundaries or in MAGs.
caveats: A predicted CRISPR-Cas locus does not prove present activity, immunity, spacer target, or editing capability.
Mobile elements, divergent Cas proteins, fragmented contigs, and mixed bins can confuse subtype assignment.
Spacer-to-target analyses require separate evidence.

documents.title: Biosynthetic gene clusters with antiSMASH

metrics.name: region/product class
metrics.meaning: Rule-based prediction that a genomic region encodes machinery associated with a biosynthetic class.

metrics.name: known-cluster similarity
metrics.meaning: Similarity to characterized clusters; it is evidence about related architecture, not proof of an identical product.

metrics.name: region boundaries
metrics.meaning: Predicted genomic interval that can include uncertain flanking genes and can be truncated at contig edges.

interpretation: Prioritize complete, well-supported regions with coherent core/biosynthetic genes and carefully interpret similarity to known clusters.
Use the embedded antiSMASH report for domain organization, gene context, and cluster-comparison evidence.
caveats: A BGC predicts biosynthetic potential, not expression, production, chemical identity, yield, or bioactivity.
Fragmented assemblies and MAG contamination can split or misassign clusters.
Novel clusters often cannot be mapped reliably to a specific product.

documents.title: Viral sequence prediction with VirSorter2

metrics.name: viral score
metrics.meaning: Model score used to prioritize sequences within the selected viral groups and configuration; it is not a universal probability of being viral.

metrics.name: viral group
metrics.meaning: Model/category supporting a candidate such as dsDNA phage or ssDNA virus under the installed database.

metrics.name: boundary
metrics.meaning: Predicted viral/proviral interval. Boundary output can be intermediate and should be refined/validated before final reporting.

interpretation: Treat VirSorter2 as a sensitive candidate-discovery step and validate candidates with quality/completeness, hallmark genes, contamination checks, and contextual evidence.
The developers recommend CheckV after VirSorter2 to refine boundaries and assess viral genome quality.
caveats: Score alone is insufficient to claim a confirmed virus or complete viral genome.
Plasmids, mobile elements, short contigs, integrated elements, and host regions can complicate classification.
Default workflows favor sensitivity and may include false positives requiring downstream filtering.

documents.title: HADEG hydrocarbon-degradation gene potential

metrics.name: orthologous hit
metrics.meaning: Sequence-cluster evidence linking a predicted protein to HADEG's curated degradation-gene collection.

metrics.name: pathway/gene coverage
metrics.meaning: Breadth of recovered components associated with a degradation route; a more coherent set is stronger genomic-potential evidence than one isolated hit.

metrics.name: network degree
metrics.meaning: Visualization property reflecting connections in the annotation network, not biochemical activity or causal importance.

interpretation: Use the network to identify coherent collections of degradation-associated genes and inspect their genome/MAG origin, completeness, taxonomy, and supporting annotations.
Describe results as encoded degradation potential or similarity to characterized proteins.
caveats: Homology does not establish substrate specificity, expression, pathway flux, environmental activity, or successful bioremediation.
Isolated hits, partial proteins, contamination, and paralogy need cautious review.
Confirm important claims with domain/context analysis and appropriate experimental or multi-omic evidence.

documents.title: Repeat and low-complexity annotation

metrics.name: masked fraction
metrics.meaning: Fraction annotated/masked as repeat or low-complexity sequence under the selected libraries and settings.

metrics.name: repeat class/family
metrics.meaning: Best supported repeat-library classification; divergent or novel elements can remain unclassified.

metrics.name: copy count
metrics.meaning: Number of reported repeat fragments/hits, not necessarily the number of intact biological elements.

interpretation: Use repeat composition and genome-map context to describe assembly complexity and candidate mobile/repetitive regions.
Evaluate repeat-rich contig edges and fragmented hits in relation to assembly continuity.
caveats: RepeatMasker is library-dependent; absence of a named repeat does not prove absence.
Fragmented assemblies can split a single repeat into multiple annotations.
Repeat annotation does not itself establish mobility or current activity.

documents.title: Genome/MAG dereplication and clustering

metrics.name: primary/secondary cluster
metrics.meaning: Groups created under configured coarse/fine similarity procedures; membership depends on thresholds and comparison coverage.

metrics.name: representative score
metrics.meaning: Tool-specific ranking combining quality attributes; it selects a representative but does not make other members biologically irrelevant.

metrics.name: ANI
metrics.meaning: Genome sequence identity across comparable regions; alignment coverage remains necessary context.

interpretation: Dereplication reduces redundant genomes for abundance/taxonomy summaries while retaining cluster membership for strain- or population-level follow-up.
Report thresholds, algorithms, quality filters, and representative-selection formula.
caveats: Clustering thresholds encode an operational definition, not a universal species boundary for every lineage.
Incomplete or contaminated genomes can distort similarity and representative selection.
CD-HIT sequence clustering and genome-wide ANI solve different similarity problems and should not be conflated.
